text:
Scottsdale mayor outlines progress on public safety, fiscal policy, and economic development
Y. S. Guinn
Mayor Lisa Borowsky announced on Aug. 12 that her administration has focused on public safety, fiscal responsibility, and economic growth in Scottsdale over the past 18 months. Borowsky said her priorities have included protecting quality of life, strengthening police and fire departments through competitive compensation, and maintaining responsible city spending.
Borowsky said recruitment and retention challenges for police officers and firefighters prompted the city to implement significant compensation improvements this year. "Investing in police officers, firefighters and emergency personnel is an investment in every neighborhood, every business and every family in Scottsdale," she said.
Addressing concerns about disruptive short-term rental properties used as party houses, Borowsky said she supported a new ordinance that strengthens enforcement against illegal commercial events in residential areas. She stated that the ordinance defines what constitutes an event center more clearly: "Residents deserve to enjoy their homes without repeated disruptions, and this action delivers another important step toward protecting neighborhood quality of life."
On fiscal matters, Borowsky highlighted the empaneling of the Citizens Budget Review Commission to provide oversight of city finances. She said her approach has reduced taxpayer burden by $84.7 million while continuing investments in public safety and infrastructure. The proposed $2.119 billion budget reflects a 3.8% reduction from the previous year’s plan with a projected reserve balance of $214.4 million.
Borowsky also pointed to investments at WestWorld of Scottsdale—including upgrades funded through low-cost financing from the Water Infrastructure Finance Authority—and initiatives such as forming a Downtown Task Force comprised of business owners to guide future planning for Old Town Scottsdale.
She outlined two recent initiatives: exploring an ordinance for large water users to ensure accountability for high-demand projects; and reviewing zoning standards specific to data centers due to their unique impacts on land use, energy demand, water consumption, noise, aesthetics, and proximity to neighborhoods.
Borowsky concluded by reaffirming her commitment: "Together we are demonstrating that it is possible to invest in public safety, protect neighborhood character, manage taxpayer dollars responsibly and grow a world-class economy at the same time."
Borowsky served as mayor after previously serving on the City Council from 2008 to 2012 where she advocated for fiscal conservatism, according to the official website. She has maintained lifelong residency in Scottsdale while supporting community service initiatives for children and older adults through board roles; resident engagement remains emphasized by regular updates from her office according to the official website.

Borowsky said recruitment and retention challenges for police officers and firefighters prompted the city to implement significant compensation improvements this year.
